rationale: This is a cosmetic one-leg swap of the archived "Rollover-Funded Capital Spending" (capx replaced by the PP&E+inventory deployment term already used in "Deployed External Capital Bottleneck"), recombining two existing components without a new mechanism, and the gross issuance/retirement double-gate mostly proxies for size/debt-intensity rather than genuine rollover stress.

Identical three-way structure to the archived "Overlevered Debt-Funded Capex Ramp" with only the investment leg swapped to the same PP&E+inventory measure used elsewhere in the archive, so it is a variant rather than a diagnosis-driven redesign of why that signal's FMB slope had the wrong sign.

The conditioning on *prior* net PP&E contraction reverses (rather than repeats) the archived "Post-Investment Financing Shortfall" sequencing and is internally consistent, though the sign is economically ambiguous since post-contraction rebuilds could equally reflect cheap, recovering assets, and the core ingredients remain the well-known investment and net-external-financing anomalies.

The residual (asset growth minus tangible deployment) decomposition with a total-growth gate is a legitimately new construction that guards against the contraction artifact, but it is close to a refinement of the published asset-growth anomaly and its residual leg is contaminated by cash accumulation, which works against the stated "opaque deployment" mechanism.

The debt-versus-equity funding flip relative to the archived "Equity-Funded Intangible Buildout" is a substantive rather than cosmetic change, the level gate correctly prevents buyback-driven false positives, and the collateralizability mismatch story is coherent—though intan-based coverage and the archived signal's near-zero alpha temper expectations.

Requiring equity issuance *and* net debt retirement alongside expansion is a genuinely different financing-composition test (net external financing is roughly neutral, so it is not a rediscovery of the composite-issuance anomaly), but it is structurally close to "Equity-Heavy Workforce Scaling," which was weak, and the triple hard gate risks a thin, unstable long leg.
